summary: Tested new Oral Peptides category end-to-end. Backend: 10/10 pytest tests passed — /api/categories includes oral-peptides at sort_order=4 with tub image serving 200 image/png; /api/products?category=oral-peptides returns exactly 8 products with valid prices (£29.99–£89.99); SLUPP combo slug 'slupp-332-250mcg-bma-15-50mcg-300mcg' resolves; existing categories (pens, vials, nasals, syringes-and-wipes, bundles) still return; admin can bump stock via PUT /api/products/{id} and revert. Frontend: header nav shows 'Oral Peptides' between Vials and Syringes & Wipes; /oral-peptides renders all 8 products alphabetised correctly (5 Amino-1MQ → BAM15 → Methylene Blue → Minoxidil → SLUPP-332 250mcg / BMA-15 → SLUPP-332 50mg → Tesofensine → Tirzepatide); SLUPP combo detail page loads, shows £74.99 and 'SOLD OUT' correctly (stock=0); all existing category pages still render.

minor.issue: 5-Amino-1MQ 50mg does NOT use the branded oral-peptides-tub.png image — it still has its old '/api/uploads/gen_d93463b2-....png'. Spec claims 'All 8 use a branded GHP-Health capsule tub image'.
stock=5 for 5-Amino-1MQ (all other 7 products correctly have stock=0). Spec says 'Stock = 0 by default'. May be leftover from previous unassigned state.
Review request references PATCH /admin/products/{id} for stock bumps, but actual endpoint is PUT /api/products/{id} (product_routes.py). Not a bug, just a spec/doc mismatch.

issues: Page-level H1/H2 shows generic 'Premium-grade research peptides' hero rather than an 'ORAL PEPTIDES' category heading. Breadcrumb shows 'oral-peptides'. Spec required 'ORAL PEPTIDES' heading. Consistent with other category pages though — those show 'Pens', 'Vials' etc., so this is a category-page heading design gap.

critical_code_review_comments: product_routes.PUT /products/{id} uses find_one_and_update but does not distinguish 'stock=0 set explicitly' from 'not provided' cleanly — pydantic ProductUpdate all-optional filter (v is not None) works correctly, verified.
Category & product endpoints correctly strip _id (doc_to_dict pattern). No ObjectId leakage observed.
